item.title: A Divided America Processes a War With Iran
item.description: As the war in Iran extends into its seventh week and a truce feels increasingly shaky, many Americans expressed bewilderment about a conflict that came with little warning.

item.title: 51 Percent of Americans Think Trump’s Military Action in Iran Has Not Been Worthwhile
item.description: A survey from Ipsos and Reuters, released on Tuesday, found few Americans — 24 percent — think the war in Iran has been worth the costs and benefits.

item.title: A New Accuser Says Eric Swalwell Sexually Assaulted Her
item.description: The woman said Mr. Swalwell, who resigned from Congress on Tuesday afternoon, raped her in a West Hollywood hotel room in 2018. She said she believed she was drugged.

item.title: Resignations of Eric Swalwell and Tony Gonzales Set Up Special Election Fights in Texas and California
item.description: Aides to Greg Abbott and Gavin Newsom were weighing whether to call quick elections to replace two House members accused of sexual misconduct.

item.title: Kevin Warsh, Trump’s Pick for Fed Chair, Discloses Vast Wealth Ahead of Confirmation Hearing
item.description: Kevin M. Warsh vowed to divest a substantial amount of his more than $100 million in assets as he faces a complicated path to becoming the next chair of the Federal Reserve.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith, Tony Romm and Steven Rich
item.media:description: Kevin M. Warsh will be at a Senate hearing next week to consider him as the next chair of the Federal Reserve.

item.title: Trump Administration Accuses Biden DOJ of Unfairly Prosecuting Anti-Abortion Activists
item.description: The report is part of the president’s effort to claim anti-conservative and anti-Christian biases in federal law enforcement, even as he pushes to wield the legal system against his political enemies.

item.media:description: The Justice Department’s efforts to end what it calls “weaponization” of law enforcement have moved on multiple tracks.

item.title: Maryland Governor and State Democrats Fail in Redistricting Effort

item.title: Virginia Governor Ends Tax Breaks for Confederate Groups

item.title: How Peter Magyar Defeated Viktor Orban, a Former Ally, In Hungary’s Election
item.description: For years, Peter Magyar was a loyal ally of Viktor Orban, the far-right Hungarian leader. Then he changed sides — and defeated his former boss in a landslide victory on Sunday. Does he represent real change?
item.dc:creator: Andrew Higgins and Lili Rutai
item.media:credit: Akos Stiller for The New York Times
item.media:description: Peter Magyar campaigning in 2024 in Viktor Orban’s hometown, Felcsut.

item.title: Will Viktor Orban’s Legacy Live On in Brussels, Even Without Him?
item.description: Viktor Orban, Hungary’s newly ousted prime minister, helped to finance a Brussels think tank that pushes his populist vision. It will outlast him, at least for a while.
item.dc:creator: Jeanna Smialek and Koba Ryckewaert
item.media:description: Viktor Orban at an European Union summit meeting in Brussels, in March.

item.title: Camp Mystic Hearing in Texas Weighs Reopening After Deadly Flooding
item.description: Testimony at a hearing this week has focused on what camp leaders knew and did as floodwaters rose in July, killing at least 116 people.
item.dc:creator: Jesus Jiménez
item.media:credit: Meridith Kohut for The New York Times
item.media:description: Generations of girls have spent their summers at Camp Mystic, nestled along the Guadalupe River in the Texas Hill Country.

item.title: A Police Chief Had a $4.5 Million Gambling Problem. No One Knew.
item.description: New Haven’s police chief, Karl Jacobson, resigned abruptly after his deputies saw red flags, including missing money. He has pleaded not guilty to embezzling city money to gamble on sports.
item.dc:creator: Hurubie Meko
item.media:credit: City of New Haven, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Karl Jacobson served as New Haven’s police chief for three years before his career unraveled.
